summary: A front page of the Bismarck Weekly Tribune for Friday, November 6, 1885, Vol. 13, No. 22, priced at five cents. The page is dense with six columns of small-type news, dominated by election returns from Tuesday's polling across multiple states — Dakota, Virginia, Kansas, New York, Connecticut, Iowa, and others — alongside a substantial column of telegraphic wire briefs under the banner "NEWS BY TELEGRAPH." A standing column of miscellaneous local and national notes runs in column one under "NEWS NOTES AND COMMENTS," and a price-summary column anchors the far right. The editorial tone is brisk and factual, characteristic of a territorial weekly aggregating wire copy for a frontier readership.
headlines: Dakota Dots and Dashes—Boiler Explosion—A Deer Hunter's Dear Shot.

clipping_placements.placement_note: under the 'NEWS BY TELEGRAPH' section head, mid-column, between Dakota political items and the Hennepin Canal brief

juxtapositions: The wire items reporting the violent expulsion of Chinese residents from Tacoma sit within the same 'NEWS BY TELEGRAPH' column as a brief on the Hennepin Canal commission and cheerful Dakota political returns, giving the expulsion no special visual weight or editorial framing.

The 'FIRED OUT.' headline at the top of column two — describing the Chinese being marched from Tacoma — runs directly beside the election-aftermath column, visually echoing the partisan 'firing out' of Democratic candidates across the region.
